tests.reason: Untestable (no way): Terminal.app 2.15 on macOS has no read that returns a cell's link. Exercised on Terminal.app 2.15 (bundle CDHash arm64 113489a0, x86_64 df446fa4) on macOS 26.6.2 build 25G83 at shipped settings, owned Mac, 2026-11-18: screen text through the scripting dictionary's contents and history; window pixels with View > Show Marks; Terminal's own line marks and Edit > Navigate > Select to Previous Mark, whose control (a keyboard prompt auto-mark) stops the selection, while after the emitted sequences the selection ran to the first line, so none left a navigable mark (this says nothing about hidden protocol state) - and the mark store is set by keyboard prompt marking with no protocol-created control, so it cannot decide this row; the accessibility tree of the window, walked completely (elements_complete true, 11 elements, every attribute, parameterized attribute and action listed), whose text area offers only AXValue screen text, selection ranges, line geometry and AXStringForRange plain text, with no attributed-string, style or mark attribute, and whose window AXDocument carries the working directory as a full file URL that follows OSC 7; the scripting dictionary (Terminal.sdef SHA256 efc515ec), whose tab properties are contents, history, processes, busy, tty and titles; and the window title and proxy icon, which show the AXDocument folder name. Across the walked accessibility tree the attribute census is 49 names, none link- or URL-shaped (AXDocument is the window's working directory, not a cell's link), and the scripting dictionary has no attribute store. OSC 8 has no query form, and the plain probe only reads the cursor, which cannot verify link metadata. This records the observation surface, not whether the app stores the link.
